skill.description: Audits domain authority and citation trust with the 40-item CITE framework, including domain-type weights, veto checks, and prioritized remediation. Use for domain credibility, GEO readiness, and citation-source evaluation; use other skills for page-level content quality or backlink-only profiling.

security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 70 static findings and found the command, traversal, URL, and reconnaissance hits to be false positives caused by Markdown formatting, repository-relative links, and metadata references. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files. Two context-level risks remain: unpinned remote reference loading and persistent storage of audit data.

remediation.suggestion: Pin fallback reference URLs to a release tag or content hash, or require user confirmation before loading main-branch instructions.
Ask for user consent before saving audit artifacts, and redact sensitive competitor, penalty, or private analytics data when possible.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Instruction Fetch
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md line 226 tells the agent to fetch the runbook and other reference files from raw.githubusercontent.com on the main branch when local files are missing. This can load future instructions that were not part of the reviewed skill snapshot.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and tied to an unpinned main-branch URL. It is a supply-chain and instruction-integrity risk, although the URL points to the author repository.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Audit Data Writes
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md lines 86-87 and 442 instruct the agent to store audit artifacts and promote veto issues into memory files. Domain audits can contain sensitive site, competitor, or penalty data, so persistence should be consented and scoped.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The memory write behavior is directly stated in the skill contract and save-results section. The risk is low because paths are fixed, but the persisted content may be sensitive.

content.user_title: Audit Domain Authority and Citation Trust
content.value_statement: Domain trust gaps can weaken search visibility and AI citation eligibility. This skill applies the CITE framework to score authority signals, surface veto risks, and prioritize fixes.
actual_capabilities: Scores domains against 40 CITE checks across Citation, Identity, Trust, and Eminence.
Applies domain-type weighting for publishers, SaaS, e-commerce, communities, tools, and institutions.
Checks veto risks for traffic-link mismatch, duplicated backlink profiles, and penalty history.
Calculates dimension scores, weighted totals, caps, and TRUSTED, CAUTIOUS, or UNTRUSTED verdicts.
Produces prioritized improvements, effort-based action plans, and handoff summaries for downstream skills.
Works with manual inputs or optional SEO, link, AI monitoring, knowledge graph, and brand monitoring tools.
limitations: Results depend on current backlink, traffic, brand, and citation data supplied by the user or connected tools.
Private platform signals, such as Search Console manual actions, must be provided by an authorized user.
It does not replace page-level content quality review; pair it with a CORE-EEAT audit when needed.
Some AI citation, knowledge graph, and IP-diversity checks may be marked unavailable without specialized data.

use_cases.title: Vet a Citation Source
use_cases.description: Assess whether a domain is credible enough to cite in content, reports, or AI answer optimization work.

use_cases.title: Prepare for a GEO Campaign
use_cases.description: Find authority gaps before investing in AI visibility, entity building, and citation acquisition.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Competitors
use_cases.description: Compare your domain against competitors using the same CITE scoring structure and priority framework.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Domain Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit with a single known domain.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit domain authority for example.com. Use the CITE framework and list the top five fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Domain Type Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate audit with a known business model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a CITE audit for example.com as a SaaS product site. Apply the correct domain-type weights.

prompt_templates.title: Competitor Comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare trust signals before planning SEO or GEO work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare domain authority for example.com, competitor-one.com, and competitor-two.com. Explain which domain is most citation-ready.

prompt_templates.title: Full Trust Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow combining domain trust, veto checks, and downstream handoff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full CITE domain audit for example.com, check veto risks first, produce a TRUSTED or CAUTIOUS verdict, and recommend the next skill.

output_examples.input: Audit example.com as an e-commerce domain.
output_examples.output: The report states the CITE score, dimension scores, veto status, and top fixes such as link quality, entity profile gaps, or review trust issues.

output_examples.input: Compare our domain with two competitors.
output_examples.output: The skill ranks domains by citation readiness, explains the strongest trust signals, and highlights the highest-impact actions for your domain.

output_examples.input: Check whether this domain is safe to cite.
output_examples.output: The result gives a TRUSTED, CAUTIOUS, or UNTRUSTED verdict with plain-language evidence and a recommended next step.

best_practices: Provide the domain type, backlink totals, top referring domains, traffic estimates, and known penalty history before scoring.
Start with veto checks so serious trust issues shape the final score and recommendations.
Pair the domain audit with content-quality review when publication, citation, or GEO decisions depend on both trust layers.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a high backlink count as authority without checking traffic coherence and link quality.
Do not compare domains with different business models without applying the correct domain-type weights.
Do not hide unavailable data; mark unknown checks clearly and explain what evidence is missing.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits domain authority and citation trust using the CITE framework across Citation, Identity, Trust, and Eminence.

faq.question: Does it need paid SEO tools?
faq.answer: No. It can work from manual data, but connected tools improve backlink, traffic, citation, and brand signal coverage.

faq.question: Is this the same as a backlink audit?
faq.answer: No. Backlinks are one input. The skill also evaluates identity, trust, eminence, veto risks, and citation readiness.

faq.question: Can it compare competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. It can benchmark multiple domains with the same scoring method when comparable data is available.

faq.question: What verdicts can it produce?
faq.answer: It produces TRUSTED, CAUTIOUS, or UNTRUSTED verdicts based on scores, veto checks, and evidence quality.

faq.question: When should I use another skill?
faq.answer: Use content-quality-auditor for page-level content quality and offsite-signal-analyzer for detailed backlink-only analysis.
